title: Normalized slice comparison for a single coefficient dual
statement: For a ringed site (C,J,R), its slice at U, independent coefficient and derived universes, and arbitrary representative-normalized duality models M,M_U [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps], let H,H_U be the actual derived internal Homs [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], O=R[0], O_U=(R|U)[0], and F the specified exact derived restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. There exist natural tensor and Hom restriction isomorphisms t and h, and a coefficient isomorphism o:F(O)≅O_U. The evaluation counit square commutes, t carries the specified Koszul symmetries to one another, and the single dual isomorphism alpha_X = h_(op X,O) ; H_U(id,o) satisfies, for every integer n, F(s(X,n)) ; alpha_(X[n]) = c_F(-n) ; alpha_X[-n] ; s_U(FX,n) ; H_U(c_F(n).op,id). The source comparisons s are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. There is no bidual or triangle assertion in this statement. The accompanying definition closedDualRestrictionIso packages this alpha naturally.

source.place: Tags 08JB, 08FI, 08J9 (equation-internal-hom), 0A97 and 03EL; representative-normalized tensor, Hom, evaluation and Koszul comparison calculations.

proof.text: Obtain the representative-normalized comparison data d. Package d.eta and d.rho as natural isomorphisms using their simultaneous naturality fields. Take o to be the canonical derived degree-zero ring restriction isomorphism. Define alpha by fixing the second Hom argument to O and transporting its value by o; its naturality follows by functoriality in the two Hom arguments.

The existing evaluation-coherence theorem gives the evaluation square for the actual fixed restriction functor. The normalized Koszul symmetries in d equal the symmetries supplied by M and M_U: compare on pure-tensor summands of K-flat representatives using tensorGenerator_ext, then transport along K-flat resolutions and tensor naturality. Substitute these equalities into the existing Koszul-coherence theorem to obtain the stated symmetry square.

Apply the normalized single-Hom source-shift restriction theorem with Y=O. Postcompose with transport by o. Naturality of sourceShift_U in its second argument moves o through the source shift. The product-functor interchange law moves the first-argument c_F(n) past the second-argument o. This is the claimed alpha formula for every integer n; it uses no biduality assertion.

proof_origin.note: Explicit source construction and categorical transport written while proving the slice clause of lem-coef-rational-bidual-triangle-compatibility.

theorem ringedSiteSignedDual_restriction
    (M : RingedSiteDualityModel.{c, v, r, w} J R)
    (MU : RingedSiteDualityModel.{max c v, v, r, w'} (J.over U) (R.over U))
    : ∃ (h : H ⋙ F ≅ ((F).op.prod F) ⋙ HU) (o : (F).obj O ≅ OU)
      (t : M.closed.tensor ⋙ F ≅ ((F).prod F) ⋙ MU.closed.tensor),
      (∀ X Y : D.{c, v, r, w} J R,
        (F).map (M.closed.evaluation X Y) =
          t.hom.app ((H).obj (op X, Y), X) ≫
            MU.closed.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom (h.hom.app (op X, Y)) (𝟙 _)) ≫
              MU.closed.evaluation ((F).obj X) ((F).obj Y)) ∧
      (∀ X Y : D.{c, v, r, w} J R,
        (F).map (M.symmetric.braiding X Y).hom ≫ t.hom.app (Y, X) =
          t.hom.app (X, Y) ≫ (MU.symmetric.braiding ((F).obj X) ((F).obj Y)).hom) ∧
      (∀ (X : D.{c, v, r, w} J R) (n : ℤ),
        (F).map ((sourceShift.{c, v, r, w} J R X n).hom.app O) ≫
            (closedDualRestrictionIso h o).hom.app (op (X⟦n⟧)) =
          ((F).commShiftIso (-n)).hom.app ((T).obj (op X)) ≫
            ((closedDualRestrictionIso h o).hom.app (op X))⟦-n⟧' ≫
            (sourceShift.{max c v, v, r, w'} (J.over U) (R.over U) ((F).obj X) n).hom.app OU ≫
            (HU).map (Prod.mkHom (((F).commShiftIso n).hom.app X).op (𝟙 OU)))
